notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Reward-Enhanced Memory in Younger and Older Adults, Julia Spaniol, Cécile Schain, and Holly J. Bowen; header citation gives 2013 and DOI 10.1093/geronb/gbt044, matching the neutral reference. This is an 11-page full primary research report with methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF path was supplied. Unassigned original/es/p fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity: journal p. 734 corresponds to canonical page 5, with pooled recognition reward main effect F(1, 71) = 19.43, p < .01, η2p = 0.22; younger-adult reward effect t(35) = 3.73, p < .01, η2 = 0.28; older-adult reward effect t(36) = 2.33, p = .03, η2 = 0.13. None was selected by numeric matching. Table 1 gives Experiment 1 younger N = 36 and older N = 37. These are mutually exclusive age groups: candidate pooled N arithmetic is 36 + 37 = 73 participants, whereas subgroup candidates are 36 and 37. No N inferred from df. These remain candidates because the locator does not select pooled versus age-specific test. Printed trial exclusions do not reduce participant N. The narrative replication verdict applies to the high- versus low-reward recognition advantage in both age groups; it does not establish the mechanism, which the authors call inconclusive. No effect-size conversion performed.
